If there's no way for us to discover truth, then what can we do? And so Jerry Bentham proposed the idea of utilitarianism. The way we understand the world is just through utility. If it is good for the majority of people, then it must be good. If it causes pleasure for the majority of people, then that policy must be good. For example, if people want to eat candy all the time and it makes them feel happy, then we should allow them to eat candy because that is inherently good.

John Stuart Mill took this basis of utility as a foundation for good and evil to create liberalism. The very idea of liberalism today is based on utilitarianism. So, for example, homosexuality: why is it good? First, homosexuals want to be who they are. Forcing them not to be homosexual would make them feel bad. Additionally, what's more important is that their actions do not harm anyone. If you just do the mathematics and recognize that allowing homosexuality brings more pleasure to the world, then you should allow it. This religious talk against homosexuality goes against the will of God and the Bible; it's just nonsense. We should focus on first principles and utility: does it bring benefit to people? This aligns very much with British philosophy, as exemplified by Jeremy Bentham.

Once this philosophy is in place, they promote scientists whose findings support this philosophy. The most famous is Charles Darwin. When his book *On the Origin of Species* came out, it was an instant bestseller and became the mainstream understanding of origins within 20 years. Despite the problematic nature of the evidence supporting evolution, science is supposed to be a field of rigorous debate. But the evidence does not explain how we think intellectually; it only explains how we got our bodies from apes.

As this alliance between the Franks and the British Empire grows, certain individuals become meeting points for these two groups. Two such people are Benjamin Disraeli and Leon the Rothschild. Disraeli becomes the first and only Jewish prime minister of the British Empire. The Rothschilds finance his banking career, and in 1844, he publishes a novel called *Coningsby*. It is not a memoir but a novel that tells the British people more about Jews because they are an exotic species in history. The book also aims to establish how Jews think.

The novel is strange but conforms to every single anti-Semitic stereotype we have today: that Jews rule the world and work together.
